record.original_question: Can the NSM parameter q be given a physical definition, with evidence, that explains the role of the number of independent random variables represented by raising a probability to the power q? Does that physical property simplify or improve the description of complex-system statistics compared with using the shape parameter or its inverse, the degrees of freedom?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In nonextensive statistical mechanics one considers a probability distribution $\{p_i\}_{i=1}^{W}$ on a finite set of states and a real parameter $q>0$. The associated escort distribution is defined by
$$P_i^{(q)} \;=\; \frac{p_i^{\,q}}{\sum_{j=1}^{W} p_j^{\,q}}, \qquad i=1,\dots,W,$$
and the Tsallis entropy is
$$S_q(\{p_i\}) \;=\; \frac{1-\sum_{i=1}^{W} p_i^{\,q}}{q-1}.$$
When $q=n$ is a positive integer, elementary probability theory identifies $p_i^{n}$ as the probability that $n$ independent random variables, each distributed as $\{p_i\}$, simultaneously occupy state $i$.

Problem. Provide a physical definition of the real parameter $q$, supported by quantitative evidence, that:
(a) explains the role of the quantity $p_i^{\,q}$ as encoding (a possibly non-integer) number of independent random variables sharing the same state; and
(b) demonstrates that this physical interpretation of $q$ simplifies or improves the statistical description of complex systems (such as those exhibiting long-range correlations, power-law distributions, or anomalous diffusion) when compared with describing the same systems through a shape parameter, or equivalently through its reciprocal, a number of degrees of freedom.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is formulated as an explicitly stated open problem regarding the physical interpretation of the nonextensivity parameter q in Tsallis statistics. While q has been linked heuristically to long-range interactions, finite-size effects, and degrees of freedom, no consensus physical definition that fulfills the stated requirements has been established in the literature, and the problem remains open as of the available sources.

status_evidence.claim: The physical interpretation of q is listed as an unresolved open problem.
